data.reasoning: Both models agree that the PKGBUILD and associated configuration files are standard and contain no malicious code. The 'inconclusive' verdict from the first model was solely due to transient API errors (HTTP 400) when reviewing .gitignore and n8n.service, not due to any security concerns. The second model successfully reviewed all files and confirmed they are safe.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement was caused by a tool error (HTTP 400 API failure) in the first model, which prevented it from reviewing two files and forced an 'inconclusive' overall verdict. The second model reviewed all files without error and found them safe.
coverage_issues: Model 1 (qwen3-235b) failed to review .gitignore and n8n.service due to LLM API HTTP 400 errors.
learnings: The audit tool should implement retries for transient API errors (like HTTP 400/500) before marking a file or the entire audit as inconclusive.

When aggregating results, a tool error in one model should not override a successful, safe verdict from another model that covered the same files, unless the failed files are critical and remain unreviewed.
